story_text.value:
There is some recent discourse about what a "better" interface for humans managing agents looks like. Email/inboxes have come up, and it's reinforcing the premise of thing i've been building. e.g.

  - https://x.com/brian_armstrong/status/2119112609223827547
  - https://x.com/rough__sea/status/2119288646671155217?a=KRzp4CnuV6SijzvCTUw&s=20
This isn't 'another ADE', this is a side-car type of experience and it integrates nearly a year of work around annotating markdown, html, other artifacts since I requested the original Claude Code Hooks feature for better human-control integration.

The email inbox model is intuitive, but so could be "forums", slack-like, or other surfaces feel right.

I do not believe we will be working in coding sessions (full transcripts) much longer. I've been hitting flow-state on top of a better surface layer to make decisions and annotate artifacts, view variations, review code, etc all feedback going back to the agents

MIT/Apache2.0:

https://github.com/backnotprop/plannotator

title.value: Show HN: Email-like interface to review, decide, and annotate agent work

story_text.value:
I've made AntiFind, to allow you to search everywhere at once, vastly increasing the efficiency of LLMs and your own searches:

AntiFind indexes filesystems, not folders.

It maintains a live view of storage by reading filesystem metadata directly. Because it understands the underlying filesystems, it can search across storage that the operating system is not currently exposing, including unmounted partitions.

Allowing you to search for and play media from Linux in your Windows and the other way around. Without mounting the drives.

This works on Linux, Windows and MacOS.

The underlying idea is simple: instead of walking directories, read the filesystem's file tables directly.

Most tools discover the filesystem again every time you search. AntiFind reads the drive's metadata in one pass and then follows changes as they happen.

AntiFind supports Windows, Linux and macOS. It includes both a GUI and a command line. The CLI supports JSON output (--json) and was designed to integrate cleanly with automation and LLM workflows.

There's a lot more to it, and you can find timings on my site, but that's the core idea.

More information: https://antisoftworks.com/antifind

Cheers!

story_text.value:
Hello HN!

I've always had a bad time redistributing programs that use shared libraries, AppImage in my opinion does too much, and a container is an overkill - not always integrates smoothly.

I've moved to nix since long ago, but redistributing between nix and other distros or vice versa it's still a pain in the ass, more so if you want to run an alien app in nix or a nix app without the package manger in any other distro.

For that, with the help of Claude, I've implemented a format that deduces at pack-time all the shared libraries a program needs, puts them, together with its own glibc and a patched dynamic linker into a single executable.

This means that you don't actually need a runtime nor any special capability, it can run inside a FROM SCRATCH docker, alpine linux etc... And it also supports coreutils-like multiple programs accessible via symlinks, so it is a good fit for that purpose.

You can just use:

> felf pack $(which git) --output git.felf

and you'll have already a git binary that works everywhere, no matter which distro you are building this from. This only packs the binary and their dependencies.

Essentially, the effect is similar as if you LD_PRELOAD's all the libraries that it requires.

In the end, we have been fighting these demons since long long ago, chroots/docker/appimage/flatpack/nix etc...

So this xkcd applies: https://xkcd.com/927/

I'm happy to share the project, I hope it inspires new discoveries/tools in this regard!

title.value: Show HN: FELF – AppImage-like single binaries without FUSE, root, or a runtime

story_text.value:
I am one of the (dozens!) of users of Stage Manager, but I don't like some of its UX choices. For example, it moves newly opened windows into a new stage, which breaks my focus.

I spent some time trying to see if I could modify SkyLight and Window Manager to tweak Stage Manager behaviors, but this required me to turn off SIP and the experience was janky.

So I built a full replacement that still feels great to use. You can make as many stages as you want, reorder them, and drag windows and apps between them. IMO all the drag-and-drop behaviors work the way you’d expect.

Like several recent window managers, emcee hides windows in an invisible Space (I learned this from yabai), and it works with SIP on. There were lots of little edge cases to get right, e.g:

  - Keeping the strip’s previews fresh without hammering Screen Recording
  - Cmd-Tab switching to the right stage and putting focus somewhere sensible.
  - "Save dialogs", listening for app quit events, etc.
Happy to answer any questions!

title.value: Show HN: emcee – macOS Stage Manager alternative

story_text.value:
Hi HN! :)

I’ve been working as a fullstack freelancer for over 4 years now. I always wanted some kind of IDE where I could take designs, turn them into code, and not be restricted to using auto layout and all that stuff.

Back at the beginning of 2020, before LLMs and AI were a thing, I was sitting with a friend of mine trying to figure out how to take a design, even one built with absolute values, and turn it into a working web app. I tried and failed :(

Today I’m launching Velork! It’s meant to be the IDE for everything frontend. You can design UIs, work in 3D, add motion, share your designs, and convert them into actual code with your favorite stack in just one click.

It also works with your current subscription, so you can bring Claude, Codex & more.

To help you get a feel for it, we’re giving away 2,000 free AI credits to every new user :)

I’m happy to answer anything about how it works under the hood. I’m also curious what you’d want an “IDE for everything frontend” to do that current tools don’t!

title.value: Show HN: Velork – Design and Code, Together

Hi HN, I'm Jeroen, and I built PlanFinder, which generates single-floor apartment layouts. You pick an outline, entrance, and walls that get daylight, and it generates layouts which you can edit.

It's using a custom discrete diffusion model, trained on mostly European floor plans. Plans can afterwards be filtered on hard constraints like minimal area, or minimum width of a space.

Curious to hear your thoughts!

story_text.value:
I built this because it was useful for me when building evals/benchmarks, and I decided to put it up for free for others. The goal was quite simple, make it easy to use a lead claude code / codex session in a panel on the side, while allowing every cell to also be a terminal session running claude/codex, and make it possible to continue a session in an actual terminal window if I needed to. They can all talk to each other using cells on the grid, named cells, or the MCP server that effectively glues the app together. I also found it useful for managing context within related but disparate sessions.

My real benchmark runs with recalc are internal to my startup, so to demonstrate some of the functionality I built a small FDA Bench with the tool (obtain and put together dossier's of FDA submissions, and see if a harnessed Claude could have accurately predicted pass/fail): https://github.com/sshah03/recalc#a-model-benchmark

It is still very much a work in progress, but given the versatility of spreadsheet apps, wanted to see how others see themselves using it and what doesn't exist that would be useful to them. Currently runs locally on macs, linux as well but that's less tested, and Windows hasn't been tested at all so that'll come in the future.

title.value: Show HN: Recalc – Spreadsheet where cells can be Claude Code or Codex terminals
